lines: ANSI C rand(): seed = seed*0x41c64e6d + 0x3039; returns (seed & 0x7fffffff) >> 16.
Seed lives at 0x11250c. Used by snake_place_food_2416f6 and rotation_handler_241fd0.
Returns the head pointer of widget list N: widget_lists_110904[class_map_2e06a9[N]*0xc].
Lists are 12-byte {head, flags,...}; widgets are 0x40+ byte nodes: +0 next, +0x1c index byte, +0x3c flags u16, +0x3e class byte, +0x40 list number.
Walk list from widget_list_head; return first node whose +0x3e class == arg0 (arg0 < 0x6b) and +0x1c index >= arg1, else the last matching node.
Callers are the games UI layer (0x2431xx..0x2438xx).
Under interrupt lock: set list flags |=1 (if head non-null) and |=2 for the widget's list (+0x40), clear widget flag bit 4 (+0x3c &= 0xffef), set ui_dirty_flag_110901 = 1. Returns 1 (0 if arg null).
Hypothesis: schedules a repaint of that widget/list.

RTOS block allocator: picks the first of 8 pools whose block size (table at [0x100020+0x14] + i*4 + 2) >= requested size, pops the pool free list; if every pool is empty it queues a delay entry and services the scheduler, then retries.
Emits diagnostic bytes to the trace port at 0x600000/0x600100.
RTOS block free: block header at ptr-8 holds pool index ^0x80; pushes the block onto that pool's free list (rtos_mem_pools_10931c + pool*0x14), wakes a waiter if one is queued.
Ghidra marks it noreturn by mistake; it returns.
Draws a bitmap descriptor {+0 bitmap*, +4 x, +5 y, +6/+7 clip offset, +8/+9 clip w/h, +10 attr}; bitmap = {+0 data, +8 width, +9 height}, PCD8544 layout (bit (y&7) of byte [x + width*(y>>3)]).
Calls lcd_put_pixel_25f32c(x, y, attr) per pixel, attr^0x10 for clear pixels. Used by snake_draw_241198 and the Memory/game3 draw paths.

widget_measure(metrics, widget): fills the widget's metrics block at +0x20 from the style tables. 0x22bcc0 picks the first 16-byte entry of 0x2d6e4c whose flags match the UI flags at 0x11fd16 and copies its geometry; 0x22c0f8 selects an 8-byte entry of 0x2d6748 starting at 0x2d6d90[widget +0x3f] (the style class) and matching widget +0x41 >> 5 (the style variant); 0x22bdb4 derives the remaining extents. Sets flag bit 1 = metrics valid, which widget_text_height_22f7fc, widget_link_243428 and widget_set_highlight_24387a test before reading +0x20/+0x24/+0x28/+0x2c/+0x2d.
This fixed the meaning of the two fields named provisionally last week: +0x3f is the style class, +0x41's top three bits the style variant; the setters were renamed accordingly.

Memory: draws the whole board. Loops rows x cols (dims in arg2[0..1]); a card byte with bit 7 set is face-up and draws its value & 0x7f, otherwise 0xff (back). Tile origin = (origin + 2*i - dim) * 4. Cursor (arg3) is drawn last with attr 0x21.
Calls memory_draw_card_240668(value, x*4, y*4, attr).
Memory: deals a board. Builds 1..0x49 on the stack, Fisher-Yates shuffles it with rand_2b64d4 % n, writes each value twice (pairs) into the board, then shuffles the board in place.

Memory: moves the cursor. arg3/arg4 select row or column deltas with wraparound via divmod_2b5388; when both are equal it steps diagonally until it lands on a face-down card. Ends with games_ui_refresh_243170(2,0).

Scheduler: cancels the delay entry of task N (12-byte task table at 0x100140). Unlinks it from the delay lists at 0x100020+0x10/+0x28, folding its remaining ticks into the successor, marks the entry state 1, returns the remaining tick count. Same structures as sched_delay_queue_insert_2699be/service_269acc.
Medium confidence on the verb; the queue mechanics are clear.

Switches the UI context byte at 0x11fd1a (next to game_index_11fd1b). If the class (table 0x2e15ac) changes and the old context is not 7, releases the old class via 0x243646(class, 0), stores the new context, then 0x2a59fc() rebuilds.
Called by the games framework at 0x263468/0x263154 when entering/leaving a game screen.

ui_slot_remove(kind): 26-slot table ui_slots_10f268 (12 bytes: +0 text id, +4 kind, +6 value/0x114, +8 flag; kind 0x1a = empty). Removes the slot with this kind by moving the last used slot over it, then 0x2a59fc() rebuilds. Counterpart of ui_slot_set_2a5e8c.

Hypothesis (unnamed): 0x2ac6fc -> 0x2b4fd6(table_2db724[ *0x11fcce * 8 ]); 0x2b4fd6 sets state at 0x1124f4 and posts 0x243646(0x67, table_2d3948[id*0x20]) or queues the id if busy. Possibly a tone/animation request keyed by the current profile; needs 0x243646 mapped first.

Allocates a 0x4c-byte widget (rtos_mem_alloc), inserts it into widget list (arg2 or class_map[class]) sorted by (class, index), sets +0x3e class, +0x1c index, clears +0x34/+0x3c, initialises via 0x2432e0, sets flag 0x20, marks dirty.

widget_set(class, index, arg, data, flags): data == 0 clears/destroys the widget (special-cases the focused class at 0x10eb48+0x11 and +0x10, frees its buffer, then 0x2431e8(class,index,0)); otherwise finds the widget by class/index or creates it, marks it dirty, stores data at +0x34 and applies flag bits (bit 2 -> +0x18 |= 0x80). Returns flags>>3.
0x243646(class, data) is the (class, 0, 0, data, 0) wrapper used by the framework and by ui_context_switch_2a5dec.
Hypothesis (unnamed): widget remove/detach; called as (0,0,ptr) to drop the focused widget and (class,index,0) from widget_set_243550.

Draws an unsigned decimal number (abs of arg0) right-aligned at (arg1, arg2): divides by 10000..1 with divmod_2b5388, blits each digit from the 3-byte glyph table games_digit_glyphs_2d96ec at x = arg1 - 4*pos - 2 via lcd_blit_bitmap_25f3b6. Leading zeros suppressed. Rotation uses it for cell values.

Rotation: draws the board (cells 6 apart in the state array, tile pitch 7x4 px) with games_draw_number_2406b6, frames the selected block with lcd_fill_rect_25eec0, and applies the rotation animation phase (arg2 1..6) as per-cell pixel offsets around the block edges. Block size comes from the level record (+4 of game_records: bits 0-1 and >>2).

game3: scores an event for lane arg0. Object type (0x1102cc[lane-1]) 1-2 costs a life (arg1--, score -25 or to 0, status 0x11 = game over at 0 lives), 3/7/8 +10, 4 +5, 5 +15 and shortens arg3, 6 +20 and sets arg2 = 6. A miss (0x1102e0[lane] != 1) just subtracts 10 if score >= 10. Score is game_records[game].score.
game3: for each of 6 lanes with no object, with probability 1-7/8 spawns one: type = rand%8 (nonzero), sub-type = rand%3+1, speed = 8 - level, x from {0x1c,0x2e,0x40}, y 8 (lanes 0-2) or 0x1b (3-5).

game3: draws the scene from bitmap descriptors at 0x2d9a24..0x2d9a78 and sprites 0x2d995c..0x2d9a20 via lcd_blit_bitmap_25f3b6. Not offered in the 3210 Games menu; behaviour matches a falling-object reaction game.

Correction: this is a menu-item enable check, not a key check. Returns 1 if item arg0 (1..16) is enabled in the current menu context: mask = descriptor (0x10bbec[0x10b2dd[*0x111931]*0xc]) bit (item-1), everything enabled when the descriptor is inactive (+9 != 0); items >= 0x11 always enabled.
Renamed ui_key_allowed -> menu_item_enabled once the callers (first/next enabled item, select item) made the role clear.

Destroys a widget: with a null pointer it looks the widget up by class/index and first calls its class handler widget_class_handlers_2e0660[+0x38](widget, 3). Unlinks the four neighbour pointers (+8,+0xc,+0x10,+0x14), removes it from its list (head or prev->next), flags later lists (+4 bit 1) for repaint, marks dirty, frees the block.

Initialises a widget from the 4-byte class map entry (widget_class_map_2e06a9 - 1 + class*4): +0x38 handler index, +0x40 list (arg1 or entry byte 1), +0x3f entry byte 2, +0x41 entry byte 3; clears neighbours and +0x18/+0x42; clears flag bit 4.

Links widget b next to widget a: relation 1 = b below a (a+0x14/b+0xc), 2 = above, 3 = right (a+0x10/b+8), 4 = left; inserts b into any existing chain and, when flags != 0, sets the corresponding bits in +0x18 (1/2/4/8, 0x10 for the flags bit 1 case). Relation 2 also runs a bounds check via 0x22c15c before linking.
First enabled item (1..count) in the current menu context; count = descriptor[+4] or [+2] depending on +9.
Next enabled item after arg0, wrapping from count back to 1; returns arg0 if nothing else is enabled.

Selects menu item arg0: if the list fits in menu_visible_rows_11fd18 it just stores the first enabled item; otherwise stores the selection (+8), adjusts the top-of-window item (+7) with next/previous enabled items so the selection is visible.
srand: stores arg0 into rand_seed_11250c (same literal as rand_2b64d4). game3_spawn_objects_242dd0 reseeds before spawning.
Previous enabled menu item before arg0, wrapping from 1 to the item count; mirror of menu_next_enabled_item_2625f2.
Row of item arg0 within the visible window: counts next-enabled steps from the window's top item (context +7, table 0x10bbf3).

Number of enabled items in the current menu (0 when none): first enabled item then 0x26263a() to count onward. Consumed by menu_render_2629d0 as the rows-remaining counter and by menu_select_item_2626f4 against menu_visible_rows_11fd18.

Maps item ordinal arg0 to its entry index in the 0x1c-byte menu entry table at 0x10b32c: starts at the context's first entry (descriptor +1) and follows the next-entry byte at entry-2, n times; returns index-1.

Refresh timer control for the games UI: arg0 == 2 -> if state (0x110902) is 2, repaint via games_ui_refresh_243170 and, when state is 1, post delayed scheduler event 0x50 (delay 0x3c3d); otherwise cancel event 0x50 if pending and store arg0 as the state.
Medium confidence on the exact state meanings.

Renders the current menu page: clears widgets 0x19-0x21, computes the scrollbar position with the software-float helpers (title widget 0x19, bar 0x1a), then for each visible row from the window top builds text widget 0x21 (and 0x1d icon / 0x1e mark 0x28/0x29 for checkable menus), links them with widget_link_243428/0x2438e8, re-paginating when rows overflow; finally highlights the selected row via 0x24387a and 0x296f4e. arg0 == 0xff tears the menu down (0x2a5e1c(6)).
Last enabled item: walks down from the item count until menu_item_enabled_2623b0 says yes; 0 if none.
Counts enabled items from arg0 up to the last enabled one (inclusive) via menu_next_enabled_item_2625f2; menu_enabled_count_26265c feeds it the first enabled item.
Position of item arg0 among enabled items (1-based): counts enabled items below it using the context's 16-bit enable mask; returns arg0 unchanged when the context is inactive.
widget_link_by_class(classA, idxA, classB, idxB, relation|flags<<8): looks both widgets up and calls widget_link_243428(B, A, relation, flags) when both exist with the right index.

Height in pixels of text widget (class, index): measures each glyph of the widget's string (+0x34 text id resolved through 0x296adc with ui_language_11fcb1, font row 0x2d223c[+0x24]) via 0x25e4fe, takes the max against +0x20>>3, adds paddings +0x2c and +0x2d. Ids 0x901..0x970 are remapped to 0xe201. menu_render_2629d0 uses it to paginate.

Fills a 15-byte style struct (arg2) for widget (class, index), creating the widget if missing: +0xc class, +5..+8 from the 12-byte style table 0x2d6568 keyed by the widget's list (via 0x243934), +0xd/+0xe from widget +0x3f/+0x41. Returns 1.

Looks the current language byte (ui_language_11fcb1) up in the 4-byte table 0x2d6548 (terminated by '*'), stores entry[2] into menu_visible_rows_11fd18 and entry[3] into 0x11fd17, returns entry[1]; default rows = 3. Explains why the menu window size is language-dependent.
Hypothesis (unnamed): resolves a menu descriptor (+6 flags, +7 index) to an item id, optionally through the remap table 0x11fc80 or by searching the entry table for a matching id.

Hypothesis (unnamed): temporarily points the context's entry table at a sub-table (0x10b2dc+0x20 + 8*n) to set widget 0x1b's text from the resolved entry, then restores it; looks like the title/softkey text for a submenu.
Sets the widget's style class (+0x3f) for (class, index), creating the widget if missing and setting flag bit 0 when the value changes. widget_measure_22c15c indexes 0x2d6d90 with it.
Sets the style variant (top 3 bits of +0x41, value * 0x20), marks dirty, clears flag bit 4. widget_measure_22c15c matches it against the 0x2d6748 style entries; menu_render_2629d0 passes 0 or 5.
Sets or clears highlight bit arg2 (0..2) in widget +0x28 bits 25..27 for (class, index), marking dirty on change; menu_render_2629d0 calls it as (0x21, selected_row, 2, 1) to highlight the selection.

Builds the menu path indicator shown top-right (e.g. "6-2-..."): for each menu level, utoa_2a3dc2 of the level's item number joined with "-" (0x2629ac); the current item number is appended, or "..." (0x2629b0) when it would not fit; for right-to-left languages (flag at 0x11fd16 bit 3, language != 0x19) the numeric groups are reversed. Result set through 0x2a5e8c(6, str). Returns early via 0x2a5e1c(6) when the context flags bit 3 disable the indicator.
strcat: appends src to dst, returns dst.
strlen.
strcpy: returns dst.
isdigit: ctype_table_2e1929[c] & 4. atoi_2b6018 tests the same table: bit 3 = space (skipped), bit 2 = digit.
atoi: skips leading space class, handles '+'/'-', accumulates decimal digits.
utoa: writes the decimal digits of arg0 (no leading zeros, '0' for zero) into arg1 and returns the digit count; divides by 10000 downward via divmod_2b5388.
Hypothesis (unnamed): dispatches through an 8-byte handler table at 0x2db720 with constant 0x5ec; menu_render_2629d0 calls it once.

Index (0..5) of menu level id arg0 in the six 8-byte level records at menu_levels_10b2fc; the path string has at most six components for the same reason. Returns the loop index in r0 (Ghidra shows void).

Ordinal of the item whose id equals arg1 within menu context descriptor arg0 (+4 flags, +5 index, +2 count, +1 first entry): flags bit 0 = direct/indirect id (bit 2 returns arg1, bit 1 maps through 0x11fc80), otherwise walks the entry chain (next byte at entry+0xe of the 0x1c-byte records) comparing entry ids; 0 if not found.

ui_slot_set(kind, value): finds the slot of this kind (or the first empty one) in ui_slots_10f268; slot type from 0x2e1479[0x2e1590[kind]*8]: 1 = text id (kept only if the string resolves via 0x296adc/0x296b74), 2 = raw byte in +6, anything else removes the slot; then 0x2a59fc(). Kind 6 carries the menu path indicator.

Stops periodic slot n: three 12-byte slots at periodic_slots_1121ac, handler table periodic_slot_handlers_2dcbdc (12 bytes: fn, u16 param, ...). Cancels delayed event 0x2c, calls handler(3, n) unless the slot is free (0x19), frees it, and reposts event 0x2c with delay 5 if any slot is still active.

Starts a periodic slot of kind arg0 with args (arg1 word, arg2 byte): takes the first free slot, copies the handler's u16 param, calls handler(1, slot) and posts delayed event 0x2c (5 ticks). Returns 0xff when all three slots are busy. menu_render_2629d0 uses the pair around the scrollbar/marquee state at 0x10b2b4+3.

Hypothesis (unnamed): phone status text builder keyed by codes 500+n (uses service_record_build_contact_pair_282afc, 0x287216/0x287730 lookups); reached from menu_render_2629d0 for one menu type. Outside the games' own needs.

Second dormant game. Event handler with the standard codes (0x49 init, 0x57 draw) and keys '*' submit, '2'/'8' cycle the symbol under the cursor, '4' copy/back, '5' pick. Mechanics are Mastermind: a secret of length logic_params_2d9760[1] (minus one below level 4) over (level&3)*2+5 symbols; guesses live in rows of 5 at logic_board_110364 (10 rows); each submitted row is scored by logic_score_guess_241cf6 into logic_row_scores_110398; 0xff (all exact) posts status 0x13 (win). Not referenced by game_table_2d9484 and never entered in any coverage run.
Name inferred from the mechanics plus the 'Logic' string in the English text block (Nokia's Logic on the 5110/6110 is this game); treat the prefix as a strong hypothesis.

Logic: draws the symbol palette row (top, when cursor row is 0), every guess row with its score pegs, a divider line at y=7, the cursor cell with attr 0x21, and the held symbol; symbols drawn with memory_draw_card_240668 (shared tile drawer).
Logic: arg0 < 0 regenerates the palette of 10 distinct random symbols (1..0x49) at logic_palette_1103b0 (duplicates are rejected by rescanning); arg0 > 0 returns palette[arg0-1]; 0 -> 0.

Logic: arg0 == 0 generates the secret (len arg1, symbols 1..arg2) at logic_secret_1103a8; otherwise scores guess arg0 against it: exact matches counted and masked, then misplaced matches among the rest; returns 0xff on a full match else exact*16 + misplaced.
Logic: scrolls the board and score arrays up one row when the last row is used (memmove by 5 and by 1, clears the freed row).
Logic: draws a row's score pegs at column arg0*8 from the packed score byte (high nibble exact = 3x2 marks, low nibble misplaced = 3x1 marks), two layouts depending on how many fit.

Rotation: rotates the selected block's contents counter-clockwise (values move top-right -> top-left -> bottom-left -> bottom-right). Block origin from the 4-byte cursor arg1 (row, col; cells are 6 apart per row); 2x2 below level 4, 3x3 ring of 8 cells otherwise.
Rotation: the clockwise counterpart of rotation_rotate_block_ccw_242754 (same block geometry, inverse cycle).

Not a function: interior of rotation_handler_241fd0 (no prologue; 0x24221e falls into it). Wraps the cursor after a move using divmod by the board size and posts tick event 0x30 with delay 3 for the rotation animation. Listed as a label so the worklist stops offering it.

Software double multiply (sign = a.sign ^ b.sign, exponent add). menu_render_2629d0 computes the scrollbar thumb as (pos-1) * ((rows-7) op c) / (count-1) with this, double_div_2b49b8 and 0x2b44f6; Snake's tick delay uses the same family.
Hypothesis (unnamed): software double add or subtract (aligns exponents, no sign combination); used once by menu_render_2629d0 on the scrollbar height.

Activates menu item arg0 in the current level: rejects items beyond the count or disabled; stores it as the level's selection (+6); if the level flags bit 6 it posts task-5 status 0x38c (or 0x38e for item 0) with the item's payload word and does not return; otherwise renders the menu (or clears the pending 0x2b4fd6(1) state). Returns 1 on success, 0 if rejected.

Enters menu level arg0 at item id arg1: after 0x262fa4() it binds the level's context descriptor (0x10bbec[...]) to the level record (0x10b2b4 + idx*8 + 0x48), resolves the item ordinal by id, applies the descriptor flags (bit 0 -> 0x263006 sets a 16-bit pair at +4/+6; bits 4/5 start/stop something through 0x24b174/0x24af00), then activates the item (falling back to the first enabled) and ui_context_switch_2a5dec(1). Posts task-5 status 0x5de/0x5eb when the level has no enabled item.
Returns to the current level's remembered selection (+6 of its descriptor) and re-activates it, stopping the 0x24af00 side effect if active; this is the 'Last view' style return after a game ends.

editor_close: if an editor is open (state block 0x110590 +8), runs its teardown (0x24adc8: cancels delayed event 0x31, destroys the focused widget, clears widget 0x29, removes UI slot 2, restores the previous UI context) and flushes pending text (0x24aedc), then sets 0x11fcd4 = 1. Menu descriptor flag 0x20 and menu_leave/menu_return call it.

Returns the n-th (arg1, 0-based) entry of menu level arg0: level record in menu_levels_10b2fc (8 bytes: +0 id, +1 first entry, +2 count), entries are 0x1c-byte records in menu_entries_10b32c chained by the next byte at entry-2; result points at entry-0x1c (record base). 0 when the level or entry is missing.
Clears menu level arg0: walks count+1 entries of its chain clearing the used flag at entry-3, then zeroes the level id.
Removes the n-th entry (arg1, 1-based, <= count) from level arg0's chain: relinks the previous entry's next byte, clears the entry's used flag, decrements the level count.

Frees level arg0: for each first entry, frees the payload pointers at +0/+4/+8 as selected by arg1 bits 0..2 with rtos_mem_free_26abf8, removes the entry, then clears the level via menu_level_clear_262218. games_menu_handler_29a144 calls it with flags 2 when leaving a game menu.
Ensures widget (class, index) lives in widget list arg2: if it exists in another list it is destroyed and re-created there (sorted insert); created fresh if absent.
widget_set_243550(class, 0, 0, data, 0) followed by widget_move_to_list_243664(class, 0, 1): post content and pin the widget to list 1.

Picks the per-list style entry for widget list arg0: starts at 0x2d6730[list] and advances while the 12-byte entry's flag byte (0x2d656c[n*0xc]) has no bit in common with the UI flags at 0x11fd16, up to the list's limit; falls back to the first. widget_get_style_2453ec and the layout pass consume the result. (Distinct from the per-widget style class/variant used by widget_measure_22c15c.)

Hypothesis (unnamed): computes a vertical extent for a widget from fields +0x46/+0x49/+0x4a and padding +0x2c, relative to a parent, when +0x28 bits 17..18 are set; part of the layout pass at 0x243ba8.

Leaves the current menu level if it is open (+0x2a of the level slot): stops the 0x24af00 effect (state 1 -> 2), cancels delayed event 0x31, tears the menu down with menu_render_2629d0(0xff, 1) unless suppressed (+1), calls 0x2ac6fc, clears the open flag. menu_enter_263154 calls it first.
Increments the current context's menu nesting depth byte (0x10b2dc[ctx*4+1]), capped at 6, matching the six level slots.

Builds the 16-bit item enable mask for the current level: for each entry (direct 0x14-byte table or the 0x1c-byte chain) reads bit (+0x1e / -10) of the byte pointed to by (+0x18 / -0x10) and packs it at the item's position. menu_enter_263154 stores it at level +4/+6 when descriptor flag bit 0 is set; menu_item_enabled_2623b0 tests it.

Allocates a free entry among the 0x50 records of menu_entries_10b32c (used flag +0x19), copies the template (arg2), and links it into level arg0's chain: as first entry when the level is empty, at position arg1 (1-based) when given, else at the end; increments the level count. Returns 1, or 0 when no entry is free.

Creates menu level arg0 in the first free slot of menu_levels_10b2fc (params arg1..arg3 at +3..+5) and inserts its first entry from a default template (payload arg4, text 0x114, 0xdc, 0xc, 0x11) via menu_level_insert_entry_2632fc; rolls the slot back when the insert fails.
Leaf: if ui_repaint_state_10eb3c == 3 set it to 2 (same transition ui_refresh_timer_243180 makes before repainting). BL target from outside the games region; callers are not in the closure.
If ui_repaint_state_10eb3c is non-zero, clears it and calls ui_refresh_timer_243180(0), cancelling the pending repaint.
Destroys the focused widget (pointer at widget_focus_10eb48, the same block widget_set_243550 consults at +0x11/+0x10) and clears the pointer.
Sets widget +0x38, the widget_class_handlers_2e0660 index, for (class, index 0). Returns 1 if the widget exists.
Sets or clears bit arg1 of widget +0x42 and marks the widget dirty when the bit changes.
Find-or-create (class, index), set flag bit 0, then set or clear the arg2 bits of +0x41 (the field widget_set_style_variant_24383c writes in its top 3 bits).
Find-or-create (class, index); an existing widget is marked dirty and, if flag bit 0 is set, re-initialised through widget_init_2432e0; then +0x38 (class handler index) is set to arg2.
Sets or clears widget flag 0x80 (hidden) for (class, index), sets flag 0x20 and marks dirty when it changes. widget_is_unobscured_2439ac ignores widgets with bit 7 set, which fixes the bit's meaning.
Returns 0 if any later widget in the same list that is not hidden overlaps this widget's rectangle (+0x47 x, +0x45 w, +0x49 y with heights +0x2c/+0x2d/+0x46), else 1.

The games UI layout and paint pass (about 0xf80 bytes, under interrupt lock): resolves each widget list's style variant, clears and repaints overlapped list regions through the per-class handlers (event 3 then 6), then positions widgets along their neighbour links with the style paddings. The entry scan split it at 0x243a50/0x243a5e/0x243ba6/0x243ba8 (false BL decodes in its literal pools); those are labelled as parts, not functions.
Not a function: interior of level_widget_callback_240604 (no prologue; the pointer scan matched a literal). Labelled so the worklist stops offering it.
Not a function: interior of the unnamed 0x2624b8 (sets widget 0x1b text for a submenu entry); labelled as a part.
Clears 0x10b2b5 and tears the menu down with menu_render_2629d0(0xff, 1).
Tears the menu down (menu_render_2629d0(0xff, 1)) when the context's open flag (0x10b2de[ctx*4]) is set.
Pops one menu nesting level: clears the current level slot, marks it state 7, restores the previous level's slot and adjusts the depth counter (max 6).
Hypothesis (unnamed): leaf that writes (arg0 == 1) to 0x110900, the byte before ui_dirty_flag_110901; a second UI flag whose reader is outside the closure.
Hypothesis (unnamed): resets cached UI tables via 0x2ae7c4 then posts task-5 status 0x5de (the same failure status menu_enter_263154 uses when a level has no enabled item).
